newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end at sixth record February close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end at sixth record February close.

text.p: Mexican stocks drifted up to their sixth record close for the month on Monday on foreign buying and ahead of expected falls in primary interest rates.
"The market responded well, buying was solid and foreign capital inflow was what helped," said a floor trader.
The leading IPC share index rose 9.73 points, or 0.25 percent, to a record close of 3,889.77. Trading volume was moderate at 74.5 million shares.
Traders said inflation figures for the first half of February had little effect on dealing as they were released shortly before the close.
Banco de Mexico announced in late trade that consumer prices increased by 0.89 percent for Feb. 1 to Feb. 15, compared with 2.57 percent for January as a whole.
A Reuters survey of financial houses in Mexico City showed they had expected an average increase of 0.88 percent.
The IPC reached an intraday high of 3,908.48 points in mid-morning trade before profit-takers stepped in.
Traders said forecast falls in primary Cetes, or Treasury bill, rates spurred early buying.
Dealers said foreign buyers were partly encouraged by a recovery on Wall Street after a downturn last week.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 1.10 percent, or 76.58 points, at 7008.20.
The most heavily traded gainer was financial group Bancomer whose B shares ended up 3 centavos (1 cent) at 3.18 pesos (41 cents) on what traders said was a technical recovery following recent falls.
Retail stock Comerci topped the decliners and was also the most heavily traded stock of the day, unseating Telmex into an unaccustomed second place.
Comerci UBC share units fell 46 centavos (6 cents) to 6.54 pesos (84 cents).
Telmex L shares ended down 2 centavos (1 cent) at 15.54 pesos ($2.00).
On the broad market, of 118 stocks traded, 60 ended up while 31 were down.
